title: Perimeter sampler bridge and opaque context proxy for VPC/on-prem observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: For Dedicated and Private deployments we need a robust way for on-prem/VPC collectors to make local sampling and routing decisions without leaking tenant-identifying metadata upstream. Current perimeter forwarders either send full context to the hosted control plane (violates isolation) or strip everything (loses trace continuity).

Goal: Build a lightweight perimeter sampler bridge that executes configurable, tenant-scoped sampling policies at the edge and a paired opaque-context proxy that preserves cross-service trace continuity without forwarding raw tenant IDs or PII. The combination should enable: local latency/error dashboards, fair sampling under noisy tenants, and safe replay/retention semantics for troubleshooting incidents in private deployments.

Scope: edge-side components (on-prem collector plugin + perimeter proxy), control-plane policy spec extensions for sampling rules, SDK wiring for opaque context propagation headers, and dashboard ingestion transforms. This scope excludes long-term storage changes or billing integrations (handled by separate work).
acceptance_criteria: On-prem collector plugin can apply tenant-scoped sampling rules expressed as rate, deterministic, and adaptive (error-biased) policies without sending tenant IDs to the hosted ingest tier.

Opaque context header format defined and documented; contains only non-identifying routing token and cryptographic provenance that hosted systems can use to reconstruct spans belonging to the same trace without resolving tenant identity.
Edge sampler respects per-tenant soft quotas and signals backpressure via telemetry metrics (noisy-tenant-drop-rate) to the dedicated control plane dashboards.
E2E test harness that simulates 10 tenants with skewed traffic shows overall trace recovery >= 95% for traces allowed by sampling policy and zero tenant ID leakage in captured payloads.
Design doc and security review completed; implementation passes threat model checklist for no-PII-in-flight in default configuration.
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial problem framing and constraints added. Assigned to Liam.

2025-02-14: Spike complete — prototype perimeter sampler implemented as a Lua filter in Envoy sidecar. Findings: rate and deterministic sampling are cheap; adaptive error-biased decisions require lightweight counters in the collector.
2025-02-21: Security review kickoff. Decided to use HMAC-signed opaque tokens rotated daily; no tenant lookup allowed in hosted plane without explicit enterprise opt-in.
2025-02-25: Design doc updated with header spec (X-RW-Opaque-Context) and state machine for token issuance and validation. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Perimeter+Opaque+Context
2025-03-01: Implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/847. Wire up tests and add sampling telemetry metrics (noisy_tenant_drops, sampler_latency_ms).
2025-03-04: UX sync with Console team (Sofia Martinez). Agreed ingestion transforms will attach tenant-agnostic tags for dashboard grouping. Added acceptance test for 95% trace recovery.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: doing sampling in the perimeter reduces telemetry volume but makes post-hoc rehydration harder; mitigated by preserving opaque context for trace stitching.
Performance: sampler must add <1ms p95 overhead on the critical path; initial Lua filter approach meets this goal in lab but will move to compiled plugin for on-prem bundles.
Privacy: header contains an opaque 16-byte token + 4-byte provenance; signed with tenant-scoped key so hosted systems can verify continuity without learning tenant mapping.
Operational: added metrics and alerting thresholds for noisy-tenant-drop-rate > 1% sustained over 5m, sampler_error_rate > 0.1%.
Next steps: finish PR reviews, create release candidate for private deploy package, run raid-style failover tests with Dedicated routing policies.
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Martinez): ensure dashboard UX surfaces when sampling reduces available traces for a tenant and provide clear explainers for customers.
Security (Rajiv Nair): recommend rotating signing keys via KMS and include key-id in header metadata; flag: support offline key validation for air-gapped installs.
Infra (Noah Wilson): prefer a compiled collector extension for memory/perf on constrained on-prem hosts; acceptable as a follow-up if prototype proves correctness.
qa_plan: Unit tests for header encoding/decoding and HMAC validation.
Integration test against synthetic traffic generator simulating 10 tenants with Pareto traffic distribution.
Fuzz test to ensure no tenant ID leakage through headers or logs.
Canary deploy to one Dedicated customer with SOC approval and monitor telemetry for 72h.
deployment_notes: Will ship as part of on-prem collector plugin release 0.12.0 and console-2025.03. Edge config controlled by 'perimeter_sampler' feature flag (default off).
Provide migration guide: how to enable opaque context tokens, key rotation steps, and how to interpret new sampler telemetry in Console.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged beta -> 2 enterprise customers -> general availability after 6 weeks and security sign-off.
